subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Circuit Breaker Pattern
description: A fast breakdown of The Circuit Breaker Pattern for builders.

hook.text: Service A calls Service B. Service B is down. A keeps trying, queuing up thousands of failed requests.

buildup.text: A circuit breaker detects repeated failures and stops calling the broken service. It 'opens the circuit.'

discovery.text: After a cooldown period, the breaker tries again. If the service recovers, traffic flows normally once more.

twist.text: Without a circuit breaker, one failed service cascades into total system failure. Everything goes down together.

climax.text: Circuit breakers protect your system by failing fast instead of hanging. Quick failure is better than slow death.

punchline.text: Stop calling dead services. Fail fast. Recover faster.

quiz.question: What does a circuit breaker do when it detects repeated failures?
options: It stops calling the failing service and returns an immediate error instead
It reboots the failing service automatically
It sends all traffic to the database instead

details.summary: The circuit breaker pattern stops an application from repeatedly calling a failing service. After a threshold of failures, the circuit opens and requests fail fast instead of waiting. It periodically tests if the service has recovered before closing again.
details.whyItMatters: Without circuit breakers, a single failing dependency can cascade and bring down an entire system. This pattern is essential for building resilient distributed architectures.
takeaways: Prevents cascading failures from a broken dependency
Requests fail fast when the circuit is open
Periodically tests recovery before resuming normal calls

faq.question: What are the three states of a circuit breaker?
faq.answer: Closed means requests pass through normally. Open means requests fail immediately without calling the remote service. Half-open means a limited number of test requests are allowed through to check if the service has recovered.

faq.question: How do you choose circuit breaker thresholds?
faq.answer: Set failure thresholds based on normal error rates so the circuit does not trip on transient errors. Timeout durations should balance between giving the failing service time to recover and failing fast enough to protect the caller. Test under realistic conditions.
